findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data
findings.body: The new call `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` at line 1024 passes an empty `data` object. Prisma's `updateMany` requires at least one field in `data`; an empty `data` either throws (`Argument data must not be empty`) or silently no-ops, and either way it does not bump `updatedAt`. That defeats the stated intent (`// Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential`), so the cache-lifecycle indicator on SelectedCalendar will silently stop being updated. Pass a non-empty value such as `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`.

findings.title: deleteCacheMutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` defined at lines 42-50 only fires `onSuccess` (toast + `onSuccess?.()` callback) but never invalidates the `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` query. After a successful deletion the dropdown still shows the old "Cache Status: Last updated: ..." line because `cacheUpdatedAt` is not refetched. The neighbouring `disconnectMutation` (lines 53-65) correctly invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`; `deleteCacheMutation` should mirror that pattern so the UI updates immediately after deletion.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (lines 173-188) groups all `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` and aggregates `_max.updatedAt` without filtering by `expiresAt >= now()`. The cache reader elsewhere (`getCachedAvailability`) only returns non-expired entries, so a credential whose only caches are expired (CACHING_TIME is 30 days) will still display a misleadingly recent "Last updated" timestamp even though the cache will never actually be served. Add a `where: { ..., expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) } }` predicate so the status reflects cache that is actively being served.

findings.title: Hardcoded 'en-US' locale for cache timestamp formatting
findings.body: Line 89 instantiates `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`, which forces en-US date formatting regardless of the user's actual locale. The component already has `useLocale()` in scope (line 37) and uses `t()` for surrounding strings, but the formatted timestamp bypasses the user's locale. Non-US users will see US-formatted dates/times for "Cache last updated". Format with the user's locale instead of hard-coding "en-US".

findings.title: In-place sed uses BSD-only syntax, fails on Linux
findings.body: Line 68 runs `sed -i '' -E "..." "$ENV_FILE"`. The empty `''` argument is BSD/macOS sed syntax meaning "no backup suffix"; GNU sed (Linux) interprets `''` as the sed script and `-E` as a positional argument, so the command fails on Linux developer machines. Detect the platform or switch to a portable form (e.g. `perl -pi -E ...` or conditional `sed -i -E ...` on GNU vs `sed -i '' -E ...` on BSD) so the script works on both.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache handler, repository methods, or component
findings.body: The PR introduces the `deleteCache` tRPC mutation and `deleteCacheHandler` (this file), `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` on `CalendarCacheRepository`, `updateManyByCredentialId` on `SelectedCalendarRepository`, and the `CredentialActionsDropdown` UI component, plus an empty-data `updateMany` call in `CalendarService.fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`. None of these additions ship with unit tests or component tests, so the empty-data `updateMany` bug and the missing-query-invalidation behavior are not regression-protected. Add at least a handler test (verifying the user/credential ownership check and the cache deletion), tests for the two new repository methods, and a component test covering the dropdown's invalidation flow.
